method: Authoring corrections triggered by actual browser walkthrough and checked against primary NICE recommendations via indexed official-source text. Direct fetches returned 403.
scope: Three new rotation cases and nr-012 model assessment

changes.before: Request an EEG first, using the limb jerks to classify the event before reviewing the witness account
changes.after: Obtain a routine EEG and arrange a first-seizure clinic assessment

changes.before: Review the event with the witness, examine for concerning features and obtain a 12-lead ECG
changes.after: Review the witness account, examine her and obtain a 12-lead ECG

changes.before: Request brain imaging first, using a normal scan to establish a reflex cause for the collapse
changes.after: Obtain a head CT and observe for delayed neurologic symptoms

changes.before: Arrange an exercise test first, using age alone to decide that resting cardiac assessment can wait
changes.after: Obtain echocardiography and arrange an exercise tolerance test

changes.before: An epileptic seizure, established by the presence of any limb movement
changes.after: First epileptic seizure with bilateral motor activity

changes.before: A ventricular arrhythmia, established by the brief loss of consciousness
changes.after: Arrhythmic syncope from an intermittent tachyarrhythmia

changes.before: An uncomplicated vasovagal faint with brief associated jerking
changes.after: Vasovagal syncope with brief associated jerking

changes.before: Postural hypotension, established by being upright before the event
changes.after: Postural hypotension related to reduced circulating volume

changes.before: Explain likely triggers and recurrence precautions, document the event and arrange appropriate follow-up
changes.after: Explain triggers, recurrence precautions and appropriate follow-up

changes.before: Begin antiseizure treatment based on the witnessed jerks and postpone discussion of the trigger
changes.after: Arrange first-seizure assessment and EEG before deciding on follow-up

changes.before: Use a routine EEG result as the requirement for all discharge decisions after this typical event
changes.after: Arrange tilt testing to confirm the mechanism before giving trigger advice

changes.before: Reassure her that the normal resting ECG excludes every future cause of loss of consciousness
changes.after: Arrange ambulatory rhythm monitoring and defer counseling until results

changes.before: Repeat seated pressure several times without asking whether symptoms occur after standing
changes.after: Measure seated BP at repeated visits and compare it with home readings

changes.before: Use the lying pressure alone because it is above the usual hypertension treatment target
changes.after: Measure lying BP in both arms and use the higher reading for interpretation

changes.before: Measure pressure lying and after at least one minute of supported standing, recording symptoms
changes.after: Measure lying BP and BP after at least one minute standing, with symptoms

changes.before: Compare pulse oximetry before and after standing as a substitute for blood-pressure measurement
changes.after: Measure heart rate and oxygen saturation during a supported standing test

changes.before: Symptomatic postural hypotension, with medication and intake as possible contributors
changes.after: Symptomatic postural hypotension with potentially reversible contributors

changes.before: A proven primary autonomic disorder, because all posture-related symptoms have one cause
changes.after: Primary autonomic failure causing neurogenic postural hypotension

changes.before: Sustained ventricular tachycardia, because a normal resting ECG confirms intermittent rhythm events
changes.after: Intermittent ventricular tachyarrhythmia causing recurrent presyncope

changes.before: An uncomplicated vasovagal faint, established solely by the absence of chest pain
changes.after: Reflex syncope triggered by prolonged standing in a warm environment

changes.before: Intensify all antihypertensive medication using only the lying pressure, ignoring standing symptoms
changes.after: Adjust hypertension therapy toward the lying BP target and review seated home readings

changes.before: Prescribe salt loading to every patient with this finding before considering comorbid conditions
changes.after: Arrange autonomic function testing before changing any current medication

changes.before: Label autonomic failure now and omit a review of the new medication and reduced intake
changes.after: Monitor home pressure for four weeks before assessing the new symptoms

changes.before: Review drugs and volume status, address contributors, reduce fall risk and reassess standing BP
changes.after: Review medication and volume status, reduce fall risk and recheck standing BP

changes.before: Close the assessment because the initial blood-pressure fall already explained every future symptom
changes.after: Continue the same plan and review symptoms at the next annual hypertension visit

changes.before: Reassess likely causes and consider specialist evaluation for the persistent symptoms
changes.after: Reassess causes and consider specialist evaluation

changes.before: Infer that the initial measurements were fabricated because symptoms did not fully resolve
changes.after: Attribute the remaining episodes to reflex syncope and arrange tilt testing

changes.before: Choose a permanent neurologic diagnosis from the blood-pressure readings alone
changes.after: Treat the pressure fall as primary autonomic failure and begin disease-specific therapy

changes.before: Classify generalized epilepsy from the bilateral movements alone and omit the cardiac assessment
changes.after: Request outpatient MRI and classify the episode from the convulsive pattern

changes.before: Use a normal current neurologic examination as proof that no seizure occurred
changes.after: Observe for another event before investigating the recovered patient

changes.before: Request a routine EEG as the only investigation and treat its result as a definitive exclusion test
changes.after: Request an urgent EEG and defer the remaining assessment until it is reported

changes.before: Review the witness account, examine her, check metabolic factors and obtain a 12-lead ECG
changes.after: Review the witness account, examine her, check metabolic factors and obtain an ECG

changes.before: An uncomplicated faint, because normal vital signs afterward settle the event’s mechanism
changes.after: Reflex syncope with associated convulsive movements

changes.before: A first suspected epileptic seizure, with onset and underlying cause not yet classified
changes.after: First suspected epileptic seizure with onset and cause unclassified

changes.before: A specific generalized epilepsy syndrome, established by one bilateral convulsive episode
changes.after: First generalized-onset tonic-clonic seizure in a generalized epilepsy syndrome

changes.before: A psychogenic event, established by the absence of a metabolic abnormality
changes.after: Functional seizure requiring assessment by a specialist in nonepileptic events

changes.before: Wait for a second event before arranging any specialist assessment or safety discussion
changes.after: Provide safety advice and request specialist review if another event occurs

changes.after: Arrange urgent first-seizure assessment with interim safety advice and indicated tests

changes.before: It does not exclude epilepsy; continue interpreting the event and any further testing in clinical context

changes.before: It proves that no later seizure can occur, so interim safety advice can be withdrawn automatically
changes.after: Recurrence risk is now low enough to withdraw the interim activity precautions

changes.before: It establishes a functional diagnosis without further history or specialist assessment
changes.after: A functional seizure becomes the leading diagnosis; arrange psychological assessment

changes.before: 45-year-old man with 18 hours of continuous acute vestibular syndrome after an upper respiratory infection. HINTS by a trained examiner favors a peripheral pattern, with an abnormal right head impulse, unidirectional left-beating nystagmus, and no skew; hearing is intact and no focal deficits are present, consistent with right vestibular neuritis.
changes.after: 45-year-old man with 18 hours of continuous acute vestibular syndrome. HINTS by a trained examiner favors a peripheral pattern, with an abnormal right head impulse, unidirectional left-beating nystagmus, and no skew; hearing is intact and no focal deficits are present, consistent with right vestibular neuritis.
